text: The boy Samuel served the LORD under Eli. In those days the word of the LORD was rare; visions were not widespread.
One night Eli was lying down in his usual place. His eyes had grown so weak that he could no longer see.
The lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was.
Then the LORD called to Samuel, and he answered, "Here I am."
He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am; you called me." But Eli said, "I did not call. Go back and lie down." So he went and lay down.
Again the LORD called, "Samuel!" Samuel got up, went to Eli, and said, "Here I am; you called me." "I did not call, my son," he said. "Go back and lie down."
Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, and the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.
A third time the LORD called Samuel. He got up, went to Eli, and said, "Here I am; you called me." Then Eli understood that it was the LORD who was calling the boy.
So Eli said to Samuel, "Go and lie down, and if he calls you, say, 'Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening.'" So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
Then the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, "Samuel! Samuel!" And Samuel said, "Speak, for your servant is listening."
The LORD said to Samuel: "See, I am about to do something in Israel that will make the ears of everyone who hears of it ring.
On that day I will carry out against Eli everything I have spoken against his house, from beginning to end.
I have told him that I am judging his house forever because of the sin he knew about: his sons were bringing a curse on themselves, and he did not restrain them.
Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the guilt of Eli's house will never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering."
Samuel lay down until morning, and then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. He was afraid to tell Eli the vision,
but Eli called him and said, "Samuel, my son." And he answered, "Here I am."
"What did he say to you?" Eli asked. "Do not hide it from me. May God deal with you, and worse still, if you hide from me a single word of all that he said to you."

versions.text: "What did he say to you?" Eli asked. "Do not hide it from me. May God deal with you, and ever so severely, if you hide from me a single word of all that he said to you."
versions.explanation: The oath formula "May God deal with you, and ever so severely" reads awkwardly aloud because "and ever so severely" is left dangling without a verb. The Hebrew idiom is "thus may God do to you and thus may he add" — a smoother rendering keeps the escalating force while flowing naturally in speech.

text: So Samuel told him everything and hid nothing from him. Then Eli said, "He is the LORD; let him do what seems good to him."
Samuel grew up, and the LORD was with him, and he let none of his words fall to the ground.
And all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.
The LORD continued to appear at Shiloh, for there he revealed himself to Samuel through his word.
